idiom: hit the nail on the head
meaning: to describe or identify exactly what is causing a problem or to say exactly the right thing
literal_translation: влучно сказати саме те, що потрібно
example: You hit the nail on the head when you said the schedule was the real problem.
origin: Comes from carpentry, where a hammer strikes the top of a nail directly so that it goes straight into the wood

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hit something with a heavy tool by accident
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the literal reading of the words. The idiom is figurative and has nothing to do with accidents or tools.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to make a loud noise while working on a building
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom does not describe noise or construction work. It refers to accuracy in speech or thought.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to miss an important detail completely
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which means being exactly right rather than missing the point.

explanation: 'Hit the nail on the head' means to describe exactly the right thing or to identify precisely what is causing a problem. It is common in everyday spoken English and in informal writing.
